description: What is on the ground at a point, in one call: the admin units, ward and pincode; land cover, elevation and slope, population density and block land use; climate zones; the river basin, nearest river, water body, dam and wetland, and flood history; hazards (seismic zone, landslides, cyclone tracks, coastal regulation zone); forests and protected areas with the nearest one; the nearest highway, railway and metro station, airport and bus stop; the nearest hospital (three sources) and school, and places within 1 km; the nearest power line, power plant and water-supply facility; distance to India's outline. Returns a one-line `summary` and `sections`, each with its credit, licence, scale, vintage and status; for the air above the point, `air` points to the mugilu MCP's conditions_at. Example: 'what is around this plot in Kolkata?' -> lat: 22.57, lng: 88.36. For a narrow question pass sections (or layers) so surface_at reads only those: one section takes about 0.1 to 0.3 s, against up to 3 s for everything, and the answer is only what was asked ('which ward is this?' -> sections: ["place"]; 'nearest railway station' -> layers: ["ir_stations"]; 'how high is it?' -> layers: ["dem"]). For a broad one ('what is at this point?', a site screening) pass neither and it reads everything. list_layers and get_layer_detail say which section reads a layer (lookups); an unknown section, or a layer the tool does not read, is an error naming the valid ones.

layers.description: Read only these layers (ids, e.g. dem, worldcover and worldpop (the rasters), ir_stations, gs_highways, or a ward layer such as wards_chennai), as well as any sections asked; default all

open_only.description: true leaves out the non-commercial layers (for commercial use); default false

sections.description: Read only these sections (an array, or one comma-separated string); default all

name: surface_at
